note: Outside the stated ICP on almost every criterion, and a good test of whether the definition means anything. He is a travelling contract worker on rotating shifts whose current assignment may end within the week — not a business owner, physician or equivalent — and the income picture confirms it: a $1,500 monthly surplus, $2,500 liquid, four credit cards carrying $3,000 of debt and a self-described poor credit score he is actively trying to rebuild. Health is not the neglected area but an active clinical situation: a doctor has given him six months before starting blood pressure medication, he gained 40 lb in a year, and he has a herniated disc plus 6-out-of-10 joint pain. That is rescue, not good-to-great, and he frames it that way himself. The one criterion he clears is the exclusion — he is 30 to 40 lb over his target rather than 50, and he is emphatically not gym-averse: ex-Marine Corps, five or six days a week of cardio kickboxing when his job allowed it, and he currently ships kettlebells to job sites. Worth flagging for the wider analysis: this is the third call in this batch where the prospect fits the programme's spirit and fails the income criterion, and the second where the stated ICP's lack of any clinical criterion leaves a diagnosed condition — here a herniated disc under active medical supervision — entirely unscreened.
